title: Ganesha and the moon.
lines: This is a story from India, about Ganesha.
Ganesha is a cheerful god with the head of an elephant.
He has big ears, a long trunk and a big tummy.
Those are sweet little balls, filled with coconut and sugar.
The mouse is what he rides on.
Ganesha rides everywhere on his little mouse.
One evening there was a party.
All over the land people made tasty food for him.
Ganesha went to visit every house.
One modak here, two modaks there, ten modaks in that house.
Ganesha ate and ate and ate.
His tummy got so fat, as round as a big ball.
It was already late when Ganesha set off for home.
The stars twinkled and the moon shone brightly.
Suddenly a snake slithered across the road.
He fell off his mouse, onto the ground.
And all the modaks rolled out, across the road.
Ganesha sat on the ground, among the modaks.
His crown was crooked and his trunk was full of crumbs.
From high in the sky the moon looked down.
And the moon began to laugh.
He didn't like the moon laughing at him.
You don't laugh at someone when they fall.
He brushed the dust off his clothes.
He looked crossly at the moon.
Moon, he said in a deep voice, you are very beautiful.
You laugh at someone who has fallen.
That's why nobody will want to look at you anymore!
Nobody could see the moon anymore.
People had no more light to find their way.
The children couldn't look at the moon before they went to sleep.
Then the moon understood that it had been wrong.
I'm sorry, Ganesha, said the moon softly.
I shouldn't have laughed at you.
He saw that the moon was really sorry.
And Ganesha had a big heart, just as big as his tummy.
But you won't always be completely round.
Every month you'll get a little smaller, until you're almost gone.
And then you'll get bigger again, until you're completely round.
That way you'll never forget what happened.
And it still happens like that today.
Just take a look at the moon.
Then Ganesha picked up his modaks.
He gave a few to his mouse, because it had worked hard.
And if you make a mistake, just say sorry.
